newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST BARLEY PRICES DOWN ON CROP OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST BARLEY PRICES DOWN ON CROP OUTLOOK.

text.p: Barley futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) went mostly limit-down on Friday due to expectations of a good crop, traders said.
"Harvesting has started and the crop looks better than it was expected," said Mihaly Otvos of OTP Forex.
The Agriculture Ministry estimated earlier 1.22 million tonnes of combined spring and autumn variety barley crop for this year compared with last year's 930,000 tonnes.
Barley prices dropped the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for July, October, December and March and finished 120 forints lower for August and down 300 for September.
Barley settlement prices were between 19,110 for July and 21,400 for March.
Milling wheat futures continued an upward correction started on Thursday after almost three weeks of falls.
Closing of short positions also contributed to the price rise, Otvos said.
Milling wheat prices rose 120 to 300 forints for maturities from Agust to May and were flat for July at 20,180 forints.
Maize was only traded for July and it rose 150 forints to finish at 21,340.
Total grains turnover on the BCE was a modest 796 lots or 344 million forints, down from Thursday's 930 lots or 393.26 million forints.
Milling wheat futures accounted for the bulk of the turnover in volume terms with 594 lots.
